Got tricked by slight misspelling of the domain name; something like supurnova.com when the real one was supernova.com. I was in a rush, not paying attention, and the fake site looked enough like the real one that it didn't set off any flags. I submitted my order after entering the credit card before I realized my mistake. Was able to get the charge reversed though, didn't expect that.

Another time I was forwarded a invoice for some Apple product or service, I don't recall now. Normally I would have followed it up but the guy who sent it to me (the CFO) had just bought a big assed Mac system that he'd handled the purchase of personally, so I figured it was a legit charge and passed it for payment. I ran into him later in the day and, in passing, asked him why he bothered to send the bill to me for approval? It turned out that it was some spam he'd received and thought that I needed to know about it and so sent it to me without providing any sort of context.

I suppose considering the literally hundreds of attempts to trick the company out of money over the years 2 close calls isn't so bad.
